title: Una escalera de implicaciones
description: Ordena cuatro proposiciones conectadas por implicaciones universales.

sources.citation: Jim Hefferon, Introduction to Proofs: an Inquiry-based Approach, material on elementary logic.
sources.note: Reference for the logical definitions. The puzzle wording and graph are original to MathGraphs.

explanation.summary: La conjunción permite concluir cada una de sus partes; agregar alternativas a una disyunción conserva la implicación.

items.title: Eliminación de la conjunción
items.description: Si ambas proposiciones son verdaderas, P también lo es.

items.title: Introducción de disyunción
items.math: P \implies P \lor R \implies P \lor R \lor S
items.description: Una disyunción verdadera sigue siéndolo al añadir otra alternativa.

en.title: An implication ladder
en.description: Arrange four propositions connected by universal implications.

explanation.summary: A conjunction lets us conclude either part; adding alternatives to a disjunction preserves implication.

items.title: Conjunction elimination
items.description: If both propositions are true, then P is true.

items.title: Disjunction introduction
items.math: P \implies P \lor R \implies P \lor R \lor S
items.description: A true disjunction remains true when another alternative is added.

title: Diferencia, conjunto y unión
description: Sigue la inclusión desde los elementos que quedan en A hasta la unión A ∪ B.

sources.citation: Jim Hefferon, Introduction to Proofs: an Inquiry-based Approach, material on sets.
sources.note: Reference for set definitions. The puzzle wording and graph are original to MathGraphs.

explanation.summary: Todo elemento de A \ B pertenece a A, y todo elemento de A pertenece a A ∪ B.

items.title: Comprueba elemento por elemento
items.math: x \in A \setminus B \implies x \in A \implies x \in A \cup B
items.description: La dirección importa: las inclusiones inversas no son ciertas para conjuntos arbitrarios.

en.title: Difference, set, and union
en.description: Follow inclusion from the elements left in A to the union A ∪ B.

explanation.summary: Every element of A \ B belongs to A, and every element of A belongs to A ∪ B.

items.title: Check element by element
items.math: x \in A \setminus B \implies x \in A \implies x \in A \cup B
items.description: Direction matters: the reverse inclusions do not hold for arbitrary sets.

title: Las dos propiedades de una base
description: Coloca la condición que implica independencia lineal y generación del espacio.

sources.citation: Jim Hefferon, Linear Algebra, chapter on vector spaces.
sources.note: Reference for the basis definition. The puzzle wording and graph are original to MathGraphs.

context.name: Familia finita en un espacio vectorial

explanation.summary: Una base cumple simultáneamente dos condiciones: es linealmente independiente y genera todo V.

items.title: Definición de base
items.math: B \text{ es base de } V \implies (B \text{ es LI}) \land (\operatorname{span}(B)=V)
items.description: Las dos condiciones juntas caracterizan una base; cada una por separado no basta.

en.title: The two properties of a basis
en.description: Place the condition that implies both linear independence and spanning.

explanation.summary: A basis satisfies two properties at once: it is linearly independent and spans all of V.

items.title: Definition of a basis
items.math: B \text{ is a basis of } V \implies (B \text{ is LI}) \land (\operatorname{span}(B)=V)
items.description: Both conditions together characterize a basis; neither one alone is enough.

title: Preimágenes de intersecciones y uniones
description: Empareja las identidades de preimagen y ordena la inclusión que las conecta.

sources.citation: Jim Hefferon, Introduction to Proofs: an Inquiry-based Approach, material on functions and sets.
sources.note: Reference for the set and function definitions. The puzzle wording and graph are original to MathGraphs.

explanation.summary: La preimagen distribuye sobre unión e intersección; además, la preimagen de la intersección queda contenida en la de la unión.

items.title: Verificación por elementos
items.math: f^{-1}(A \cap B)=f^{-1}(A)\cap f^{-1}(B),\quad f^{-1}(A\cap B)\subseteq f^{-1}(A\cup B)
items.description: Para cada x en X, ambas afirmaciones se reducen a pertenencia de f(x) a los conjuntos del codominio.

en.title: Preimages of intersections and unions
en.description: Match the preimage identities and arrange the inclusion that connects them.

explanation.summary: Preimages distribute over unions and intersections; the preimage of the intersection is contained in the preimage of the union.

items.title: Elementwise verification
items.math: f^{-1}(A \cap B)=f^{-1}(A)\cap f^{-1}(B),\quad f^{-1}(A\cap B)\subseteq f^{-1}(A\cup B)
items.description: For each x in X, both claims reduce to membership of f(x) in codomain sets.

title: Base y coordenadas únicas
description: Conecta la definición de base con la unicidad de coordenadas y la independencia lineal.

sources.citation: Jim Hefferon, Linear Algebra, chapter on vector spaces.
sources.note: Reference for basis and coordinate results. The puzzle wording and graph are original to MathGraphs.

context.name: Familia finita en un espacio vectorial

explanation.summary: Ser una base equivale a que todo vector tenga coordenadas únicas respecto de esa familia, e implica independencia lineal.

items.title: Existencia y unicidad
items.math: B \text{ base de } V \iff \forall v\in V,\ v=\sum_i c_i v_i \text{ de forma única}
items.description: La generación da existencia; la independencia garantiza que la representación no se repite.

en.title: Basis and unique coordinates
en.description: Connect the definition of a basis to unique coordinates and linear independence.

explanation.summary: Being a basis is equivalent to every vector having unique coordinates in that family, and it implies linear independence.

items.title: Existence and uniqueness
items.math: B \text{ is a basis of } V \iff \forall v\in V,\ v=\sum_i c_i v_i \text{ uniquely}
items.description: Spanning gives existence; independence guarantees the representation is unique.

title: Intersección, conjunto y unión
description: Ordena tres conjuntos mediante inclusiones que se comprueban por pertenencia.

sources.citation: Jim Hefferon, Introduction to Proofs: an Inquiry-based Approach, material on sets.
sources.note: Reference for set definitions. The puzzle wording and graph are original to MathGraphs.

explanation.summary: Todo elemento común a A y B está en A; todo elemento de A está en la unión.

items.title: Prueba por pertenencia
items.description: La inclusión es universal y no necesita que los conjuntos sean distintos o no vacíos.

en.title: Intersection, set, and union
en.description: Arrange three sets using inclusions that can be checked by membership.

explanation.summary: Every element common to A and B belongs to A; every element of A belongs to the union.

items.title: Membership proof
items.description: The inclusion is universal and does not require the sets to be distinct or nonempty.
